dedupe_keys.name: carbon mapper data portal methane and co2 super emitter plumes from tanager 1 emit and airborne sensors

description: Carbon Mapper, a non-profit, runs an open data portal of methane and carbon dioxide super-emitter observations around the world. The data page, read on 2026-09-26, says observations come from several sensors on aircraft, satellites and other space-based systems and are added on a frequent, ongoing basis. Sources include the Tanager-1 satellite built by Planet with technology from NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, NASA's EMIT sensor on the International Space Station, and airborne campaigns with NASA's AVIRIS and Arizona State University's Global Airborne Observatory. The portal is a map with filters, a source list, summary statistics and a downloads panel, and a product guide, data FAQs and a quality control document are published. Developers register an account to use the Data API and a STAC API. Data are free for non-commercial use by governments, facility operators, non-profits, journalists and researchers under the terms of use; commercial use or redistribution needs contact with Carbon Mapper. Caveats: detections capture large point-source plumes at overpass times, not continuous emissions. Simulation uses are finding leaking oil and gas facilities and pipelines for hazard exposure and resilience analysis and checking reported emissions. Related records: data-unep-imeo-eye-on-methane publishes validated satellite plumes and company data.
